reviews.text: A chewy drama about family dynamics, sexuality and ego featuring two brothers on a ranch in Montana in 1925.
reviews.author: Christina Newland

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog is a film of uncanny beauty and subtle power, whose biggest asset is the curious interplay of contrasts of all kinds: physical power vs. powers of intellect,  innocence vs. corruption, honesty vs. hypocrisy, and love vs. hate.
reviews.author: Diana Tuova

reviews.text: Not since Lady Macbeth (2016) has a film shifted power dynamics by exploring gender, class, and sexuality in each scene.
reviews.author: Sarah Vincent

reviews.text: Much has already been said about Jane Campion's western masterpiece, and for good reason. It is indeed truly great. Benedict Cumberbatch gives a career best performance.
reviews.author: Dave Giannini

reviews.text: ...as tense and evocative as any horror movie.
reviews.author: Greg Carlson

reviews.text: An Incredible Movie with Incredible Performances
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog is a thought-provoking, deep study of (toxic) masculinity surrounded by exceptional performances and truly stunning cinematography.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: When The Power of the Dog ends, there is an immense desire to immediately start it from the beginning to see the puzzle pieces that were laid out for the audience. To appreciate the movie in a new way, from a bird’s-eye view, knowing how it ends.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: ‘The Power of the Dog’ is emotional and complex, as the movie shows the meaning of masculinity in the American Western, and how terrifying it is.
reviews.author: Nuha Hassan

reviews.text: This unique western has a slow pace that works because it is so intentional and essential to the direction of the plot.
reviews.author: Brett Doze

reviews.text: A master class in tension and survival tactics, The Power of the Dog is a film to soak up then meditate over.
reviews.author: Jennifer Bisset

reviews.text: Campion’s new Western shares a visual vocabulary with Brokeback Mountain, but what looks like an unlikely love story turns out to be a tale of revenge.
reviews.author: Brandon Taylor

reviews.text: Each of them is a victim of patriarchal policing and patriarchal violence, and each of them perpetuates it, passing that diseased rope around like a noose.
reviews.author: Noah Berlatsky

reviews.text: Benedict Cumberbatch gives his best performance to date as the soft speaking, intimidating rancher...
reviews.author: Brian Susbielles

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog will challenge its viewers. If that challenge is accepted, Jane Campion rewards cinephiles with a film that submerges you into its complex characters and themes and is one of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: David Gonzalez

reviews.text: What’s so invigorating about this dynamic is that it avoids the easy theory that the homophobe is just gay himself. Instead, The Power of the Dog casually observes that anyone can be both a monster and a victim.
reviews.author: Juan Barquin

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog explores how societal oppression has the unintended consequence of turning marginalized into oppressors with striking results and a rousing visual narrative.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: Campion’s work is so well-calibrated to the point where the sickening end of one character’s arc feels inevitable, while the hopeful conclusion for others feels tainted with an acidic air despite the promise of a better future.
reviews.author: Mitchell Beaupre

reviews.text: Jane Campion's first film in over a decade is a Western in which the only terse standoff involves its opponents trading musical notes instead of gunfire and the central cowboy duel is one that sees him wrestle with his conflicting emotions.
reviews.author: Gayle Sequeira

reviews.text: With The Power of the Dog, Campion is at the height of her skills trotting into her latest mesmerising musing on strength, desire and isolation.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: A psychodrama that cleverly writes over the masculine myths and the cowboy cults which have dyed the fabric of American civilisation. Poking plenty of holes in it, Campion tells a story about desire and denial.
reviews.author: Prahlad Srihari

reviews.text: A parable about how illusory civilizations really are ... while we are wilder and more mysterious than we want to believe. It’s also about how that wildness, when suppressed, leads to distortions more threatening than insufficient architectures of order.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Overstreet

reviews.text: Exciting, intense and so elegant... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: Engenders traditional psychological portraits of a Western, subdued yet complex, and elevates them into abstract terrains. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Elsa Fernández-Santos

reviews.text: From Johnny Greenwood’s magnificent score to Ari Wegner’s haunting frames, The Power of the Dog barks its supremacy through and through.
reviews.author: Shikhar Verma

reviews.text: Cumberbatch and Dunst shine in an unforgettable anti-Western.
reviews.author: John Paul King

reviews.text:
A gentle rhythm that advances by presenting the characters traits, and the situations they experience with a certain parsimony and remarkable subtlety.
[Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Hugo Hernández Valdivia

reviews.text: When all is said and done, "The Power of the Dog" ultimately reminds us of what Westerns have been saying for over a century, that life is "solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short."
reviews.author: Eve O'Dea

reviews.text: THE POWER OF THE DOG is a visually stunning, wonderfully played western drama, which unfortunately disappointed me a little bit in its psychological complexity and depth.
reviews.author: Jimmy Cage

reviews.text: Jane Campion turns Thomas Savage's semi-autobiographical novel into pure film poetry. The film is more essay than script and is an amazing thesis on the limitations of power as defined by the masculine vocabulary.
reviews.author: Alachia Queen

reviews.text: Campion understands that the experience of this movie for each character was a different one  a psychological horror, a hopeful tale of redemption, maybe even a dawning appreciation  and each one gets the end they were always headed to.
reviews.author: Zosha Millman

reviews.text: A brutal meditation on masculinity.
reviews.author: Jourdain Searles

reviews.text: The film’s ambition leads to confusion. Again, the ending is murky. A lasso soaked in anthrax is something new in a western, it has to be admitted, but getting to that point was a slog, a slow crawl to the Oscars.
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: It is a playful thesis if nothing else, but its rhetorical obviousness does drain the film of some subtlety in its second half.
reviews.author: PJ Nabarro

reviews.text: Call it the anti-Brokeback Mountain.
reviews.author: David Reddish

reviews.text: Campions cautionary tale on the dangers of toxic masculinity remains compellingly relevant to the present.
reviews.author: Elaine Cho

reviews.text: Campion traces the ambiguity of her characters, destroying stereotypes, and displaying the range of colors that reveal the essence of human behavior. Full review in Spanish
reviews.author: Gisela Savdie

reviews.text: It's a tough watch at times, but not necessarily in the ways you think it's going to be. It challenges you, it defies your expectations, and it fights for empathy and compassion for difficult characters.
reviews.author: James Marsh

reviews.text: Jane Campions suspenseful western explores alcoholism and toxic masculinity through a story of transformation visually connected to the internally claustrophobic atmosphere in a vast landscape
reviews.author: Amanda Mazzillo

reviews.text: Jane Campion proves once again she is a master of directing and writing and Ari Wegner establishes herself as a brilliant cinematographer.  With a bit more editing, it would have been a masterpiece for the ages.  As is, it's the best film of the year.
reviews.author: Julia Swift

reviews.text: Cumberbatch is the catalyst and a terrifying one, but there are layers to Phil's relationship with his brother, sister-in-law, nephew, himself, and figures from the past, that Campion peels away and reveals so deliberately and subtly.
reviews.author: Adam Kempenaar

reviews.text: The main attraction is Cumberbatch, whos never been better. Theres no scenery-chewing here. Phil is a snarling, egotistical sociopath who survives on intimidation. Hes toxic masculinity poured into dirty ranch cloth.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: Traces of the feminine are scattered through the film: a garden flower, a paper rose, a nesting family of birds. More than embellishments, these small but potent images are talismans of potential rebirth, reminders of hope.
reviews.author: Elissa Suh

reviews.text: With finely tuned performances, Campion and her crew craft a western stripped to the bone, under which they find a beating heart as tender as it is cruel.
reviews.author: Marya E. Gates

reviews.text: "Its a quality of Campions sterling labyrinth of a screenplay (adapted from Thomas Savages 1967 novel) which gives 'The Power of the Dog' the prickliness of a slow-burn thriller even as it never loosens the grip on its character-study reins."
reviews.author: David Lynch

reviews.text: The film might have good intentions but simply never takes the next step to become something relevant, important or great.
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: Benedict Cumberbatch is extraordinary in this subversive and spellbinding western, exploring masculinity and its oppressive impact on society. Full Review in Spanish
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: In beautiful, disturbing, and confronting ways, The Power of the Dog compels viewers to see beyond the surface and recognize that people can be optical illusions - a double image hidden in plain sight.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog makes a case that such dissection is still possible, and the resultant effort can reveal fathomless depths of analysis that can dismantle the flawed fetishization of the American cowboy.
reviews.author: Wesley Lovell

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog is a remarkable character study that sees through its leads hardened exterior.
reviews.author: Christopher Cross

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog is meticulously crafted and wonderfully executed. ...Campions film is both resplendent and morose. The Power of the Dog is a towering achievement, and the finest work of both Campion and Cumberbatchs careers.
reviews.author: Mark Johnson

reviews.text: Campion uses its tropes and our expectations to tell it mainly through visuals and through the tiniest gestures and reactions. The movie requires patient attention, otherwise its mini-explosions might look like a lot of nothing on the screen.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: Enthralling, uncomfortable, brutal and beautiful, Jane Campions first feature in twelve years is a formidable psychodrama that constantly zigs where you think it will zag.
reviews.author: Steph Green

reviews.text: "Aa sour, cruel, unpleasant picture, the kind of revisionist genre work that critics love and audiences hate."
reviews.author: Neal Pollack

reviews.text: False fronts and concealed identities poison lives and thus communities like a virus...
reviews.author: John Beifuss

reviews.text: A fairly anodyne western that only presumptuously employs its aesthetic values to demystify the toxic masculinity of the most stereotypical man of the west. Full review in Spanish
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: There are few things in the world better than a kinky Western.
reviews.author: Jason Shawhan

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog is exquisite cinematic storytelling... A Western only in its setting, with no shootouts but no less intense, characterization astute, conflicts psychological.
reviews.author: Diana Cheng

reviews.text: ...an exceptional study in character...and one of 2021's best films.
reviews.author: Michael Ward

reviews.text: Campion weaves the erotic, the Gothic, and closeted homosexuality together into a beautiful yet tragic mosaic about internal gay struggles.
reviews.author: C.H. Newell

reviews.text: I came into The Power of the Dog expecting something that would knock me flat, and I wound up shrugging it off.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: While The Piano remains a haunting exploration of female desire, The Power of the Dog is a long-delayed contemplation on masculinity from the female eye, both about repression and control.
reviews.author: Namrata Joshi

reviews.text: Filmed with stunning scenery, Dog can subvert your early opinions about who is "good" and "evil" in the drama, and make you reconsider your sympathies by the end. The movie is quietly, sneakily stunning.
reviews.author: Steve Murray

reviews.text: In Campion's subversive new western, the filmmaker's fascination with the myth of masculinity unfolds in 1920s Montana.
reviews.author: Kathryn Reklis

reviews.text: The director has gotten fine performances from Jesse Plemons, Kirsten Dunst, and Kodi Smit-McPhee, but her failure to rein in Benedict Cumberbatch, whose bellicosity becomes absurd, knocks the film sideways.
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: This film's grave was dug before filming began. Brutality for brutality's sake.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: There are many mysteries buried here, but perhaps the biggest one is "why has it taken Jane Campion 12 years to make a new feature film?".
reviews.author: Matt Neal

reviews.text: It's Home on the Range by Ingmar Bergman.
reviews.author: John McDonald

reviews.text: It's a slow build, and for most of the time, I had no idea where this was all heading - which only made its shocking but well-earned ending all the more gratifying.
reviews.author: Shannon Keating

reviews.text: embeds its powerful story of repressed desire, barely concealed psychosis, and toxic masculinity within that most fabled and revered of American genres-one that the film systematically dismantles
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: A quiet but exquisite film from Jane Campion, featuring superb performances from its cast. There's an unsettling mood and tension permeating every minute that lingers even days after the end credits rolls.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: Campion's incongruous plot twists can pass for profundity in an era ignorant of both American history and film history.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: Power of the Dog is an excellent film that you must see. Campion and her crew deliver a shockingly morbid story.
reviews.author: Ana Yorke

reviews.text: An unusual take on the western genre supported by excellent performances.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: Jane Campion's first feature film in over a decade was well worth the wait; literary, visually sumptuous, quietly intense, and brilliantly acted throughout.
reviews.author: Shaun Munro

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog marks a triumphant return to cinema for Jane Campion, proving to be a psychologically intense and emotionally beautiful experience about male machismo in the American West.
reviews.author: Harris Dang

reviews.text: It's a sad world dominated by a distorted patriarchy. Champion probes the roots of this with surgical precision and psychological acuity as if she were picking the scab off of a long festering wound.
reviews.author: James Greenberg

reviews.text: Jane Campion's western is defined by a singular presence that will linger in the audience's mind. Benedict Cumberbatch plays Phil...
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: Benedict Cumberbatch's great role in The Power of The Dog places him as one of the favorites for the Best Actor Oscar. Great Netflix original movie, with good performances also by Jesse Plemons and Kristen Durst. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alvaro Corujo

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog is at once a raw skewering of patriarchy - and its associated facets and how it manifests: power, cruelty, jealousy, manipulation, sexual inhibition, and mockery of anything feminine.
reviews.author: Akhil Arora

reviews.text: Jane Campion knows how to work the camera to great effect.
reviews.author: Marie Asner

reviews.text: A portrait of how toxic masculinity is a mask worn by small, insecure men whose greatest fear is that the world will discover their cowardice. [Full review in Portuguese.]
reviews.author: Pablo Villaça

reviews.text: Had viewers been allowed in on the ruse just a bit longer, the denouement could have been uncommonly satisfying, rather than merely amusing.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: Requires time to absorb and digest, and in that very quality it exhibits its excellence and extraordinary depth. (...) Long-awaited return to cinema of one of its greats.
reviews.author: Milana Vujkov

reviews.text: ...the admittedly clever plot threading is unfulfilling; it's not enough to balance Phil's accountability... a thin revenge fantasy masquerading as a thought-provoking exposé.
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: Director/screenwriter Jane Campion's first feature film in more than a decade, "The Power of the Dog," is a shatteringly beautiful return to form, a prickly tale of strained family bonds in the not-so-old West.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: Despite being a laborious task to watch, this is an incredibly gorgeous piece of cinema.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: Jane Campion's first feature in 12 years, is well worth the wait. A creepingly sinister drama set in 1924, the film is an exceptionally well made yet conservatively restrained historical piece.
reviews.author: Nathaniel Bell

reviews.text: Cumberbatch continues to spread his wings in terms of character choice and the boldness of a particular role.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: Right at the point that director Jane Campion should have pushed us all the way to the edge of our seats with fever-pitch intensity in The Power of the Dog, she pulls back to the solemnly serious. Just give us the melodrama, Jane!
reviews.author: Eileen Jones

reviews.text: Putting all this together, the film gains its power from a mix of fine production values and solid, but unsettling, psychological insights.
reviews.author: Robin Holabird

reviews.text: Cumberbatch embodies a character who buries his insecurities and pain beneath a veneer of machismo. He is a guarded man, keeping others at an emotional arm's length. He gets satisfaction from the pain he inflicts because it lessens his own.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: In spite of a complicated, tragic ending, it was a chore to watch, and the theme of repressed homosexuality did not help bring it to life.
reviews.author: Hannah Brown

reviews.text: Methodical. Deliberate. Decisive. Striking. Pulverising. The Power of the Dog resonates with clarity and exactitude. The emotional wallops here are stunning, and lasting.
reviews.author: Andrew Kendall

reviews.text: One of the finest screen performances of this or any year.
reviews.author: Bill Newcott

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog may be among the most unsettling films of the year, as well as one of Jane Campion's career-best. This is a highlight of 2021, and not a film to be missed.
reviews.author: David Fontana

reviews.text: I'm not sure that The Power of the Dog totally adds up, but its individual equations are often so riveting as to carry us along on a wave of pure creativity.
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog is essential viewing for cinema fans, a brilliant example of a non-Western Western and another stellar entry in award-winning Campion's canon.
reviews.author: Tori Brazier

reviews.text: With a great cast, fantastic score, and breathtaking environments, The Power of the Dog is a film worth watching.
reviews.author: Tyler Carlsen

reviews.text: One of Jane Campion's most subtle and disquiet dramatic works. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Bonfil

reviews.text: An overwhelming psychological thriller. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emiliano Basile

reviews.text: [A] brilliant and haunting piece of filmmaking...[a] tale of how we too often tear others down because we can't stop tearing ourselves apart...harsh but beautiful, unforgettable but unforgiving ... exquisitely isolating.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog features some of the best performances you'll see all year with gorgeous cinematography, a fantastic ending, and an almost horror movie-like atmosphere proceeding over the entire enterprise.
reviews.author: Kaitlyn Booth

reviews.text: While the movie offers little in the way of catharsis, it's an undeniably powerful experience, as stark as those hills from the first shot.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: Campion handles such psychological denseness with virtuoso control, often whittling scenes to snippets of emotion and innuendo.
reviews.author: Ela Bittencourt

reviews.text: Jane Campion's film quietly sneaks up on you if you're willing to settle in with it. She's the kind of director who wants the audience to do part of the work without forcing every emotion and action on to us.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog gives an unflinching and riveting portrait of toxic masculinity, homophobia, and family tensions. Even though the movie is set in 1925 Montana, the themes are universal and timeless ... It's intriguing cinematic art.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: It's not your typical shoot-em up Western, by any means. It's a sophisticated arthouse piece that requires avid thought and attention.
reviews.author: Lisa Johnson Mandell

reviews.text: The film opens with an air of "There Will Be Blood" before morphing into full-blown "A Streetcar Named Desire," then flirts with "Call Me By Your Name" before landing somewhere between "The Beguiled" and "Basic Instinct."
reviews.author: Neil Morris

reviews.text: It's not subtle, with certain objects taking on blunt, heavy symbolic weight - paper flowers, cigarettes, a saddle, a rawhide lariat, shadows on hillsides. But it has a tense, unsettling power as it moves towards an unexpected ending.
reviews.author: Alison Gillmor

reviews.text: Campion has lost none of her potency, using the landscape, and even the earth itself, to tell this primal, feral story.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Campion is a master director, more about poetry than cinematic energy. An uneasy watch but a destructive investigation on feminism and family...but ultimately all a chore to watch.
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: Without the complex layers to Phil's character and motivations, it might have been just an exercise in endurance, but it was a breathtaking and suspenseful human mystery instead.
reviews.author: Asia Frey

reviews.text: We're talking about this when it comes to awards season.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: Campion treats the material with such well-mannered reverence that you begin to wish that not just the characters, but she too, would loosen up a bit.
reviews.author: Amber Wilkinson

reviews.text: A deadset awards magnet, and it all starts with the incredible acting on display.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: Jane Campion's eighth feature film, her first in 12 years, The Power of the Dog reconfirms the director as a powerful force in contemporary cinema.
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog has an elemental grandeur more suited to its setting than its psychology. But that's the sort of filmmaker Campion is. A master of mood and manipulation, she demands we see the forest and the trees.
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: The well-defined performances of Jesse Plemons, and even more so those of Kirsten Dunst and Kodi Smit-McPhee, should not be overlooked. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Brenda Medel

reviews.text: Dynamite performances... this movie is visually is visually arresting.
reviews.author: Lonita Cook

reviews.text: [Cumberbatch] takes the mildly unlikable part of his superhero character from Doctor Strange and cranks it up several notches. Campion believes viewers will find this portrait of an abusive leader compelling -- and she is correct.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: The cast is impressive, most notably Cumberbatch... is unexpectedly brash and imposing here, and Smit-McPhee, the boy in Cormac McCarthy's The Road, is vulnerable but with a steely resourcefulness.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: The acting is sensational and Campion caps it off with a perfectly unsettling conclusion.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: The sense of foreboding is very strong in the early parts of the film, but it becomes less a thing to dread, and more a subject of fascination near the end. That is when I realized it was headed in a different direction than I expected.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: A sample of great cinema at its best. Uncomfortable, harsh and, at the same time, delicate, which does justice to a historical genre full of timeless classics.
reviews.author: Víctor López G.

reviews.text: A nuanced exploration of toxic performative masculinity and the repercussions of repressed sexual desire that will quite literally eat you alive.
reviews.author: Jeanmarie Tan

reviews.text: One of the most evocative, ambiguous and accomplished films of this year. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandro G. Calvo

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog is a successful film on many levels and a superbly realized adaptation.
reviews.author: Hugues Porquier

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog is impressive with great performances, beautiful cinematography and a compelling script.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: Though a good half-hour longer than it needs to be, this atmospheric and nuanced western finds the grim reality of the 1920s mid-west. With a clutch of outstanding performances, it feels authentically harrowing, though its plot is markedly unsensational.
reviews.author: Ben Turner

reviews.text: It's not difficult to see why this film is attracting awards speculation - it's elegant, sinister, and grand. It's the work of a master.
reviews.author: Amanda Jane Robinson

reviews.text: A period drama of meticulous craftsmanship. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Victor Esquirol

reviews.text: Campion is on point with The Power of the Dog.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: Startling performances...a triumphant return to form for Campion.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: Overall, The Power of the Dog probably isn't as powerful or wrenching as Campion intended for it to be but it remains an unsettling piece of cinema.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Director Jane Campion is a force to be reckoned with... The Power of the Dog is simply put a masterpiece.
reviews.author: Raquel Stecher

reviews.text: A magnificent work. The Power of the Dog works so beautifully because it's incisive about human behavior.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: Campion's elegant western drama is a masterful slow burner that grabs you and doesn't let you go until the very end. Benedict Cumberbatch's best performance yet. One of the year's best. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: The sort of film that reminds us what's possible when a visionary filmmaker with a polished script works with craftspeople and actors all at the top of their game.
reviews.author: Lisa Trifone

reviews.text: Trust me when I tell you, it's even better the second time around...That's when the true genius of Jane Campion shines even brighter.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog is a cinematic triumph; one of the best films of 2021. It is vivid, intriguing, contemplative, entertaining, and capped off with one of the most discussable endings in recent memory.
reviews.author: Deirdre Crimmins

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog, Campion's newest film in 12 years, is among the year's best.
reviews.author: Kathleen Sachs

reviews.text: This dark character study is beautifully crafted and skillfully acted.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: Broken into chapters, it starts as a nicely observed period piece, darkens into a psychological drama, then becomes an exercise in dread.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: Excellent support from Dunst in her best role since Melancholia and secret weapon Smit-McPhee make this a film that doesn't just have one of the year's best performances; it has four of them.
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: The film is terrific at telling a traditional story about aggression without showing traditional aggression.
reviews.author: Jon Negroni

reviews.text: Each of the characters appear refreshingly complete. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: Cumberbatch brilliantly brings to the screen 'one of the most compelling and vicious characters in American literature.'
reviews.author: Brandon Judell

reviews.text: This is where Campion feels at home: in the elusive mysteries of desire. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sergi Sánchez

reviews.text: Propelled by a remarkable performance by Benedict Cumberbatch, 'The Power of the Dog' is a visually gorgeous examination of cruelty motivated by hidden desire and retaliation driven by an impulse to protect.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: There is a monster at the heart of Jane Campion's The Power of the Dog, but I do not think the monster is the character everyone else seems to think it is.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog is a film that requires patience, but it's well worth it for its beauty and Cumberbatch's stellar performance.
reviews.author: Nicole Ackman

reviews.text: It gives a body hope for the future of cinema.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: A well-crafted film that digs deeply into the emotional lives of two brothers.
reviews.author: Harvey S. Karten

reviews.text: By capturing Phil's dangerous petulance and haunting vulnerability, Cumberbatch makes the character worthy of both our revulsion and our compassion.
reviews.author: Bennett Campbell Ferguson

reviews.text: Cumberbatch is too good to be sidelined, no matter what the pacing. This is one of the great villainous turns; a masterclass in bringing the charisma and cunning of a character -- who is himself playing a role -- to life. It is inspired casting.
reviews.author: Harry Guerin

reviews.text: As seen by the way Peter and Phil's fraught relationship is at once infused with tenderness and violence, hope and contempt, Campion's masterful filmmaking could have easily held more in the frame.
reviews.author: Rebecca Liu

reviews.text: John Ford by way Pier Paolo Pasolini, at once classical and revisionist, seductive and terrifying, a giant of modern cinema reiterating her mastery on a grandly intimate canvas.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: Campion's sinewy saga ostensibly feels like a Western before it turns into something entirely else.
reviews.author: Kent Turner

reviews.text: A masterpiece.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: Cumberbatch giving a titanic performance reveling not simply in the character's grandstanding moments but also in those in which Phil lets his guard down and we're able to see him as vulnerable and, ultimately, somewhat sympathetic.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog is a nuanced exploration of toxic masculinity that skillfully subverts expectations; a rare masterpiece.
reviews.author: Kshitij Rawat

reviews.text: This is the finest film of the year ... so far.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: The film is a cinematic pleasure, there's so much to appreciate as Jane Campion is at the top of her game here.
reviews.author: Sarah Knight Adamson

reviews.text: An exacting drama about masculinity, toxic and otherwise.... The strong performances and the striking visual style make this a potent piece of filmmaking.
reviews.author: Gary M. Kramer

reviews.text: A cinematic study on what it means to be "man", defying conventions, challenging the stereotypes of characters & its audience, leaving a bittersweet taste [Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Rivera Rubio

reviews.text: How do we know Benedict Cumberbatch is a serious thespian? Because we have no idea who he is offscreen. He's just entirely the role he's playing at any given moment, and those roles change radically.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: "Dog" is not without its faults, but its power is hard to deny.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: I haven't felt this immersed by a western since The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford.
reviews.author: Kyle Pinion

reviews.text: Every actor does such compelling work - Jesse Plemons even moved me to tears at one point - but this film belongs to Benedict Cumberbatch.
reviews.author: Natasha Alvar

reviews.text: "The Power of the Dog'' is armed with a clear message surrounding toxic masculinity, abuse, and abandonment which Jane Campion steers to pasture, creating a vivid landscape viewers will get lost in.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: Campion's masterfully crafted and acted historical drama explores both the myth of the American dream and toxic masculinity and elevates the work of a Western author who deserves posthumous praise.
reviews.author: Sandie Angulo Chen

reviews.text: "The Power of the Dog" builds tremendous force, gaining its momentum through the harmonious discord of its performances, the nervous rhythms of Jonny Greenwood's score and the grandeur of its visuals.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: What Campion does is nothing short of astounding. Everything is there, neatly wrapped into complex but carefully-handled moments.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: Some may watch The Power of the Dog and see a film that has much to offer. I, on the other hand, see a baffling narrative made only slightly watchable because of the pretty scenery and a fiery performance by Cumberbatch.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: A picturesque, enthralling exploration of male ego and toxic masculinity, crafted by an extremely talented woman and offering enough nuanced bite to keep it interesting till the very end.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: Cumberbatch has occasionally dallied with the dark side. Not even his Dominic Cummings in Brexit, though, is as repellent as Phil Burbank.
reviews.author: Ryan Gilbey

reviews.text: This may not sound like a particularly enjoyable experience. But thanks to the brilliance of both Campion and Cumberbatch, it's exquisite agony.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog - like all of Campion's work - mixes the sublime and the surprising, art walking steadily toward a wholly unexpected conclusion.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: "The Power of the Dog" licks more cigarette wrappers in dramatic confrontational establishments than Denis Villeneuve lifts and lands flying vessels in "Dune."
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: Oscar-winning filmmaker Jane Campion delivers a sophisticated adaptation of Thomas Savage's 1967 novel. Her screenplay makes each character distinct in this Americana tragedy.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: Jane Campion adapts Thomas Savage's novel with a keen focus on details. She crafts the central character not with broad strokes but with precision and finesse.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: A collection of characters and connections are delicately played to pull the audience into an intriguing web of desire, expectation and legacy. And while much of the big emotion is under the surface, the film still packs a vivid punch.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: These small touches are often where this film drums loudest, and this is down to Campion's orchestration, executed here with masterful composure.
reviews.author: Hilary A White

reviews.text: What makes Cumberbatch's performance memorable is not simply the spectacle of uber manliness which the actor had to practice and physically embellish. It's the moments when loneliness and longing break through the armor.
reviews.author: Amy Taubin

reviews.text: It's another reminder that Campion remains one of this generation's finest filmmakers.
reviews.author: Richard Propes

reviews.text: Campion's screenplay is taut, with no wasted words or flowery ruminations.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: Worth seeing just just to watch Cumberbatch strut around in spur-laden cowboy boots and perpetually dirty clothes as he delivers his lines with no trace of a British accent.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: It's an epic about the way the male id can crush everyone it touches, anchored by a brilliant masquerade of a performance by Cumberbatch, his best yet.
reviews.author: Esther Zuckerman

reviews.text: Jane Campion's first feature film in 12 years is a disquieting meditation on power, sexuality and ownership, featuring Benedict Cumberbatch in a masterful performance sure to divide.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: Jane Campion's ethereally suspenseful, unpredictable, revisionist Western features ominously glowering Best Actor contender Benedict Cumberbatch, along with slyly edgy Kodi Smit-McPhee - plus Kirsten Dunst and Jesse Plemons.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Cumberbatch turns in the performance of his career as Phil, a creature of greed and spite so pronounced that he makes Daniel Plainview seem cuddly by comparison.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: A gorgeous-looking picture undoubtedly at the artier end of the western spectrum.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: The complexity of Phil Burbank's character is played brilliantly by Cumberbatch, leaving the audience conflicted on how to feel about him.
reviews.author: Lucy Buglass

reviews.text: Sensuality and violence are intertwined in this dark, twisty, compelling and very handsome alternative western by a master female filmmaker
reviews.author: Jane Freebury

reviews.text: As a reminder of Campion's mastery of craft, The Power of the Dog is second to none; there is no one better at linking landscape and mood and performance at the most intuitive level.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: An exceptional character study, as each of the players expand upon the instincts of who they are as they clash with each other, and story is energized by their performances.
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: Although not presenting the classic unreliable narrator trope perse, it is a film that is able to pull the rug from underneath its audience in the most perfect way.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: A Jane Campion film with touches of her Oscar-winning "The Piano," a potential nod or two to Ang Lee's much-admired "Brokeback Mountain," and enough dysfunctional family forces to call its own.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: The weathered earth tones of Campion's subdued colour scheme conceal a vivid and full-blooded emotional palette.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: Director Jane Campion returns to feature filmmaking with a dark Western contrasting beautiful scenery and ugly behavior.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Dunst packs a lifetime of hurt into a handful of moments as Rose...
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: If it's a Western at all, Power of the Dog is one that springs from primal urges that lurk and threaten. It's a film that insists on being felt as much as contemplated. And feel it, we do.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: It has a lot of layers to it, and it takes its time. But it challenges the look at what it means to be a man, a woman, an adult. There's a lot of stuff built in this movie.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: It's a good, modern western, albeit one that feels more like art and less like the truly haunting tale it could have been.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: Jane Campion's The Power of the Dog could also be called The Power of Benedict Cumberbatch, as he's so spectacular.
reviews.author: Deborah Ross

reviews.text: Campion has crafted a striking Western with all the leathery textures of the genre, but with the assured and probing touch of an auteur.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Campion, who shockingly hasn't made a feature since 2009's Bright Star, crafts a compelling tale that connects viscerally with the audience and sticks its devastating landing.
reviews.author: Thelma Adams

reviews.text: Intelligently written and masterfully directed, with a near-perfect cast and a compelling story line that verges on the mythological while keeping its dusty boots firmly on the earth.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: One of this year's most haunting, well-executed films.
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: Cumberbatch does his richest film work here -- as does Dunst -- though he's more at ease as the relaxed, avuncular Phil schooling his protegé than as the cruel oppressor.
reviews.author: Graham Fuller

reviews.text: A gorgeous work of art.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog may in the end be more a twisty psychological thriller than a transcendent frontier epic. But the film's shape-shifting transformation is also part of its ruthless finesse.
reviews.author: Jake Coyle

reviews.text: New Zealand's reigning arthouse queen might seem an unlikely candidate to revive the western, but in her first feature in 11 years, Campion has created a film as powerful in its way as [John] Ford's finest.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: Not a dog's dinner - but lacking the power it thinks it has.
reviews.author: Emily Fairbairn

reviews.text: Cumberbatch is superb (what an unexpectedly good baddie he makes) but Campion deserves most of the credit...
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Campion's film reveals itself to be a piercing study of toxic masculinity and the repressed desires that can fuel it.
reviews.author: Courtney Small

reviews.text: Campion's tightly crafted tale explores all manner of masculinity, upending more than a few of our expectations along the way.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: The narrative here feels somewhat underdeveloped, but Campion remains a master of sensory storytelling, delivering a scorching study of masculinity rooted in fear.
reviews.author: Beth Webb

reviews.text: Jane Campion's The Power of the Dog zigs when you think it is going to zag, which truly is refreshing. Cumberbatch and Dunst give the best performances of their careers.
reviews.author: Lauren Bradshaw

reviews.text: Benedict Cumberbatch gives the best performance of his career-and the best by any performer this year
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: As was the case in Thomas Savage's novel, as The Power of the Dog progresses, the film acquires the traits of a thriller that Campion allocates with enormous subtlety. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Andrea G. Bermejo

reviews.text: ... a handsomely mounted Western drama about isolation and unresolved grief that's sometimes difficult to watch but even harder to shake.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog, eighth feature film by the Oscar-winning New Zealand filmmaker Jane Campion, belongs to that strange category of films whose hidden meaning is defined in his last scene. Sometimes even in his last image.
reviews.author: Ernesto Diezmartinez

reviews.text: A rich, rewarding film. It may abandon all subtlety when it comes to exploring its characters, but is so elegantly constructed you can't help but find intriguing nuances upon looking closer.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: Working halfway round the world, Campion has fashioned a startling translation of later chapters in the American creation myth.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: Cumberbatch's performance dominates most of the film's showier aspects with a sneering and malevolent presence he has managed to summon before, but under a director who uses this to amplify the film's character dynamics.
reviews.author: Jim Ross

reviews.text: Rather than watching the film, the viewer is invited to dive into it. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Martínez

reviews.text: In recent years the original book has been compared to Brokeback Mountain. But while this is also a tale of repression, desire, and homophobia, in Campion's hands at least it is more cruelly ironic than poignantly tragic.
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: Benedict Cumberbatch, Kirsten Dunst and Kodi Smit-McPhee are phenomenal, delivering entirely on the haunting, mesmerizing heart of this story. Everything from the art department to the costuming is flawless.
reviews.author: Kate Rodger

reviews.text: The movie begins and ends with Smit-McPhee. Plemons plays the most winning character. And Dunst gets the most to do expressively. But Cumberbatch dominates the film.
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: Through it all, Campion remains in masterful control of the film's obscurely menacing mood, and of every aspect of its craft.
reviews.author: Dana Stevens

reviews.text: A film that initially seems too schematic gains in complexity as the characters add dimension and Campion uncorks one gripping setpiece after another.
reviews.author: Scott Tobias

reviews.text: This is just Campion's third film as director in the past two decades, and here she makes it count - The Power of the Dog is head-and-shoulders above most 2021 movies.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog is a calculated and conflicting mind game, where the dynamics of differing personalities clash out on the range.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: Deliberate is the word that comes to mind with Campion's dialogue and direction of superb performances, especially by Cumberbatch.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: Campion works with a sure touch and epic sweep.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: This western-themed study in masculinity is built around a plot revelation so obvious and drawn out it dulls the impact of the more intriguing and macabre twist it ultimately builds towards.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: The Power Of The Dog divulges its secrets in deliberate, measured fashion, growing richer with each new reveal.
reviews.author: Katie Rife

reviews.text: An unbearably tense masterpiece, delivered with snarling intensity.
reviews.author: Ann Lee

reviews.text: [A] powerful and tragic adaptation of Thomas Savage's 1967 novel.
reviews.author: Richard Whittaker

reviews.text: Campion's disturbing, unsettling film is crafted to perfection - from the performances to a near-Shakespearean finale.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog isn't so much driven by its narrative as it is by the characters and an intense central performance.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Hums along on a single frequency of psychosexual tension without a huge amount of actual dramatic energy.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: A well-acted, beautifully shot, noir-like, grim slog, featuring some remarkably unsympathetic characters.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: Once again demonstrating her own strong, clear vision - not to mention superb control of her craft - Campion proves her ability to illuminate hidden truths and let us see what was hiding in plain sight all along.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: "The Power of the Dog" lays out this theme pretty bluntly, in a story that can feel a mite thin. It's also well worth your time, because it imagines the time, place and people it's about so intriguingly.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: Campion's emphasis on small moments...evokes the way memories work, allowing us to piece together a narrative from even the most disparate of events.
reviews.author: Ryan Silberstein

reviews.text: The game of wits between Phil and everyone else is a chilling one to watch, and it's exactly the kind of end-of-the-year movie to finish things with a bang.
reviews.author: Monica Castillo

reviews.text: Campion doesn't get the endeavor to a completely satisfying close, but she's strong with actors and composition, presenting an unnerving presentation of masculinity and desperation.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: It's a unique ride of a movie, beautiful and disturbing and haunting - in other words, it's a Jane Campion film. Here's hoping we don't have to wait 11 years for the next one.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: Do not be misled by the setting into construing this movie as a Western. It's more of a chamber piece with chaps, largely roam-free, and you soon realize that it ain't going anywhere.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog is a made with artistry and command: it is one of Jane Campion's best.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: A film that has such a necessity in its scripting, and one that commands your undivided attention throughout (and lingers with you long after), Jane Campion's The Power of the Dog is undoubtedly one of the year's best films.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog ... [is] an exquisitely crafted and generally superb character study.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: The mystery of the seen and unseen lies at the heart of "The Power of the Dog," Jane Campion's brilliantly acted, insidiously gripping adaptation of Thomas Savage's 1967 novel.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: Keeping the audience off balance, writer-director Jane Campion creates a slow, ominous build around the fine performances toward a satisfying conclusion that nicely pays off on the slow-canter ride.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: "The Power of the Dog" is a beautifully composed work by a filmmaker at the height of her powers. It deserves our attention.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: Something far stranger and more seductive than its synopsis might suggest, a hothouse psychodrama about performative masculinity and the personas we put on so as not to feel so alone.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog features gorgeously shot cinematography and splendid performances in Jane Campion's 1925-set Western.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: Campion draws it with expert precision, every detail we need to know to understand what's happening lingering in our subconscious as organic rather than convenient.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: Cumberbatch practically sears the screen with his vicious unkindness-and a complexity that hints at fragility, a degree of refinement and intelligence, despite his grimy fingernails, coarse personality and stiff backbone.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: Benedict Cumberbatch and Kirsten Dunst deliver the performances of their careers, and in a righteous world, Jane Campion will start a streak for female filmmakers winning the Best Director Oscar
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Jane Campion's purposeful psychodrama is of a time, but its power, for those paying attention, is timeless.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: Like in all films, details matter; however, in the case of Campion's The Power of the Dog, if you allow yourself distraction, if you hesitate to engage for even a moment, you will be as lost as an unguided herd on the prairie.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: There hasn't been a performance this crucial to a Campion film since Holly Hunter in The Piano.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: Brilliant! All Best Actor awards belong to Cumberbatch for this daring and unforgiving performance. Transcends acting into real life.
reviews.author: Victoria Alexander

reviews.text: The film coils with repressed rage as it nears the finish line, culminating in a final scene which puts the preceding two hours in a new light.
reviews.author: Steve Erickson

reviews.text: Campion plays the drama close to the chest, letting unspoken secrets eat away at her characters like so much rotting rawhide. Ripe with menace, the movie shifts and slides into the darkness.
reviews.author: Luke Goodsell

reviews.text: The film frustrated me a bit because it's as cryptic and taciturn as a cowboy itself, but it does feel heavy and it's nice to sink into.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog is a movie I'm certain to be thinking about a lot in the coming days, if not for the rest of the year. Jane Campion has crafted a sterling film that everyone should see the second they get a chance.
reviews.author: Terence Johnson

reviews.text: Can Jane Campion's western about toxic masculinity and repressed sexuality win Netflix its first Best Picture Oscar? Let's just say that no list of the year's best movies will be complete without this cinematic powder keg.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Cumberbatch is a force to be reckoned with in his nomination-bound role.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: Being that this is a Campion film, events and characters soon overtake their influences and we ease into a long, dark, mysterious and satisfying meditation on the human condition -- especially as it relates to blood and kin.
reviews.author: Paul Byrnes

reviews.text: You'll keep waiting for the axe to fall...and it doesn't...and it doesn't...and the tension builds to the bursting point.
reviews.author: Sherin Nicole

reviews.text: a masterpiece of psychologically intricate subtext unfolding within the majesty of the American West.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: It has seeds of ideas about the secrets we carry, repressed emotions, masculinity and clinging to the past. Still, nobody seems to water them to blossom into a work with any lingering effects. All bark with little bite.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: What Jane Campion has delivered with 'The Power of the Dog' is nothing short of cinematic perfection. It's a mesmerising work of the highest order.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: There's no point thinking you know what's coming next in Jane Campion's masterful Western drama featuring a never-better Benedict Cumberbatch as a rancher skilled at surgical bullying.
reviews.author: Linda Barnard

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog is a slow-burn and a film of many, many layers.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog is often unpleasant and tense in terms of its narrative, but that's offset by the sheer joy of watching great cinema unfold.
reviews.author: Nathaniel Rogers

reviews.text: With great direction, Jane Campion explores power dynamics and male psychology... [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ricardo Gallegos

reviews.text: Campion's take on the Western is an elegant, sometimes unnerving accomplishment.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: A slow-motion act of brutality.
reviews.author: Tom Beasley

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog features stellar work from its entire cast, and tells a story more interesting than most star-driven films out there, but it also feels like a bit of a missed opportunity.
reviews.author: Elena Lazic

reviews.text: Jane Campion serves up a nervy psychodrama set against an astonishing cattle country backdrop with impressive performances from Benedict Cumberbatch and Kirsten Dunst, but an obvious plot trajectory that dulls the storytelling impact.
reviews.author: Hanna Flint

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog, for all its pretty posturing, keeps its characters at arm's length, rattling off emotions instead of feeling them deeply.
reviews.author: Emily Wheeler

reviews.text: Campion's The Power of the Dog is unflinching in its depth and analysis, visually stunning, captivating, and bolstered by exceptional performances.
reviews.author: Mae Abdulbaki

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog ranks as the best work Campion has ever done, surpassing even The Piano.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog is a haunting psychological drama from director Jane Campion that boasts a career-best performance from Benedict Cumberbatch.
reviews.author: Lewis Knight

reviews.text: Beautifully shot, but straightforward to a fault. Frustrating.
reviews.author: Evan Dossey

reviews.text: Upending the rawhide masculinity of turn-of-the-century Montana, The Power of the Dog's seeping venom sneaks up on you in an arresting slow burn.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Zhang

reviews.text: No moral to the story. No life lesson. But, you will enjoy the view.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: Jane Campion's bold cinematic interpretation of Thomas Savage's novel (...) is a sensuous, aestheticized Netflix release, whose meticulous detail and gay subplot are admirable but a little tiring.
reviews.author: Deborah Young

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog bristles with longing and jealousy, at once staring straight ahead and sneaking up behind you, leaving its clues like muddy bootprints tinged with sorrow.
reviews.author: Shelagh Rowan-Legg

reviews.text: We frequently ask what is happening, where is this leading, how can this ever-souring situation be resolved? Rest assured that you are in safe hands with a filmmaker who has once again achieved something quite extraordinary.
reviews.author: Matthew Anderson

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog holds so much within its lens it can be overwhelming. A masterpiece in acting from Cumberbatch, Kodi Smit-McPhee is also outstanding but the true star is that of Jane Campion. An essential film.
reviews.author: Sarah Cook

reviews.text: Doggone it, just give [Cumberbatch] the Best Actor Oscar now.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: A contender for one of the year's best films, The Power of the Dog is sure to retain its strength come awards season.
reviews.author: Stephanie Archer

reviews.text: Unnecessary ponderousness, dressed up with lots of period detail. Oscar voters often confuse failing to get to the point with importance, especially if the movie looks pretty.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: Campion's genius is in keeping this crucible cooking at just the right temperature, with the perfect ingredients, stirring it the correct number of times, until it explodes.
reviews.author: Frank J. Avella

reviews.text: Each member of [Jane Campion's] wounded foursome reflects a different aspect of the tainted promise of the West. But Phil, played magnificently by Cumberbatch in a role that's completely against type, is the furious engine of the film's heartbreak.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: This really isn't one that's going to give people the warm fuzzies on a cold winter's night, but as a revenge story, it simply couldn't be more satisfying. Again and again Campion shows us how lucky we are to have her.
reviews.author: Rich Juzwiak

reviews.text: Campion is at the top of her game too. Her unflinchingly lush lens and her impressive ability to articulate even the most complex shades of human emotion mean Savage's novel could not have landed in better hands.
reviews.author: Emma Badame

reviews.text: Campion's long-awaited return to the medium of film...feels apt for a director who has demonstrated prowess at crafting an atmosphere of acute disquiet.
reviews.author: Brianna Zigler

reviews.text: Campion's modern Western presses against a razor-thin membrane between gentleness and cruelty, acting both as a searing exploration and a gorgeous tapestry of the little, secret moments that make up a person
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: For a cinema culture of late that likes to flash its intentions like traffic signs, it's refreshing to see a drama treat its audience with a little more respect for their intelligence.
reviews.author: Soham Gadre

reviews.text: Only in the skilled hands of a director like Jane Campion could the ambitious project be brought forth in such an impactful way.
reviews.author: Carey-Ann Pawsey

reviews.text: Campion is absolutely masterful in dissecting these characters subtlety... with an optimum mix of intensity and restraint.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Jane Campion's script is brilliant and absorbing, at once a stinging character study and a mystery that maintains its suspense until the final second.
reviews.author: Monica Reid

reviews.text: Jane Campion's beautifully mysterious revisionist western is a brooding, mesmerizing and masterful accomplishment
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: At a time when everything is about to change, Campion lashes out at the immobility of those who cling to ancient rituals. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Elsa Tébar

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog is something you watch with the knowledge that you're back in a trusted master's hands, safely ensconced in craftsmanship that is meticulously hewn.
reviews.author: Tomas Trussow

reviews.text: The film looks at times like a stiff-jawed period piece, but it ripples underneath with a prickly modern sensibility.
reviews.author: Chris Barsanti

reviews.text: As a translation of mood and tone, Campion is peerless. But The Power of the Dog falters some on a sheer story level.
reviews.author: Marshall Shaffer

reviews.text: Because Campion plays her hand so slowly, The Power of the Dog keeps us off-balance as to the true nature of the tension; it's the rare drama where it's legitimately hard to know what's coming next.
reviews.author: Adam Nayman

reviews.text: Superb direction, a carefully calibrated screenplay and an excellent supporting cast make this awards catnip.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: Jane Campion's beautifully shot (in New Zealand) parable goes to extreme places and builds insurmountable tension in lifelike ways, and is deeply haunting.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: For her first film in 12 years, Campion has made a magnificently performed and precisely controlled picture.
reviews.author: Reyzando Nawara

reviews.text: Campion demonstrates mastery of both what is spoken and what is seen, how words delivered with exquisite, just-so composition and deadly-true execution become, at the moment of their sublimation, images in the mind like witchcraft.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: Well-acted and richly visual.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: [Its] themes of isolation and toxic masculinity are an ever-tightening lasso of seemingly innocuous events, and they import more horror and meaning on every closer inspection, corralling viewers under an unforgettable spell.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: It's not the most propulsive narrative but manages to maintain interest due to its simmering tension, strong performances, and thought-provoking subtext.
reviews.author: Reuben Baron

reviews.text: To say that Campion's work is bad would be unfair and impartial, it is more apt to say that it is a mediocre film dressed as one of those larger than life films. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge (JJ) Negrete

reviews.text: It is a worthy return to feature directing by Jane Campion and a thoroughly relevant film to our modern discourse.
reviews.author: Andy Howell

reviews.text: Campion's slow-burn refuses to conform to any conventions of narrative, backed by a career-best performance from Benedict Cumberbatch.
reviews.author: Ian Thomas Malone

reviews.text: Jane Campion's impeccable direction illuminates nuanced and bold strokes while simultaneously redefining the Western as we know it.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: This is not a sexy film of repressed longing, it's more like fancy emotional torture porn for the literary crowd.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: Insisting on the significance of its themes, the film dispenses one emotion at a time while it creates a pervasive atmosphere of dread. Yet there's no air in the atmosphere, not much life in the brooding landscapes.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: The way this film is organized leaves it ample room to disappoint and defer, in order to make up in brief moments of iconographic pleasure.
reviews.author: Michael Scoular

reviews.text: A visually stunning and emotional story with intense thrills that are sure to surprise. Cumberbatch gives a powerful performance and is the standout of the film.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: A profoundly satisfying puzzle of masculinity that is enthralling up to the last shot.
reviews.author: Anna Swanson

reviews.text: Stunning and equally moving
reviews.author: Kathia Woods

reviews.text: Campion builds the tension slowly and emphatically, telegraphing the perils ahead. Yet when the two-edged climax comes it's powerfully unexpected.
reviews.author: Kate Taylor

reviews.text: ...a first-class adaptation that lingers in one's mind long after the credits have finished rolling.
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: Jane Campion's quiet-yet-menacing neo-Western is fantastic.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

reviews.text: The Power of the Dog packs a punch. Even beyond its across the board awards potential, it's just compelling cinema.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: [An] American masterpiece.
reviews.author: Zhuo-Ning Su

reviews.text: A subtle film that invites audiences to immerse themselves into the layered characters, "The Power of the Dog" is another stunning Jane Campion piece
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: There's rarely a moment that doesn't feel racked with the queasy, thrilling promise of sudden violence or epiphany.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: A beautifully crafted movie with some individual scenes that are some of the tensest I've experienced in some time.
reviews.author: Glenn Kenny

reviews.text: Cumberbatch wrangles an earth-shattering performance, perhaps his best ever, with an excessive bravado that seems to consume Phil from within. The intolerable fire of his repressed truth comes out as resentment.
reviews.author: Carlos Aguilar

reviews.text: Benedict Cumberbatch and Jane Campion, take a bow.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: Campion is a master of intertwining character and plot, so that a revelation of one nudges the other along.
reviews.author: Sophie Monks Kaufman

reviews.text: Campion preserves the simplicity of Savage's prose with the understated ease of her own storytelling, and she even finds a compelling way to navigate the novel's somewhat outdated dime-store Freudian conceits.
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: Beautifully shot by Ari Wegner, this is Campion at her darkest, at least as far as her narrative filmmaking goes.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: The film is not bad nor is it great, it's just underwhelming average.
reviews.author: Ben Rolph

reviews.text: A masterful excavation of the cracks and wrinkles of masculinity, and the ways that men hide from themselves in order to conform.
reviews.author: Tom Bond

reviews.text: It's cinematic poetry, if there ever was one, bourgeoning in meaning the more you linger in its shadow.
reviews.author: Tomris Laffly

reviews.text: This is a movie as big as the open sky, but one where human emotions are still distinctly visible, as fine and sharp as a blade of grass.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: It's a film which shimmers with intelligence, and if the plot isn't clear until the very last scene, well, it's worth the wait.
reviews.author: Nicholas Barber

reviews.text: It centres on a career-best performance from Cumberbatch, by turns sly and blistering, which perhaps feels all the more extraordinary since it's hard to imagine him even being cast in the first place.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: If The Power Of The Dog isn't the absolute killer coup that Campionites might have hoped, this is her most thoroughly conceived, consistently involving drama for years...
reviews.author: Jonathan Romney

reviews.text: This is a very sly and deceptive affair.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: The film's secrets are revealed while new ones bloom into being.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: A complex and probing adaptation of the late Thomas Savage's superb 1967 novel about two very different Montana rancher brothers caught in a twisted emotional bind.
reviews.author: Todd McCarthy

reviews.text: Jane Campion makes a thrilling return with The Power of the Dog, a work as boldly idiosyncratic, unpredictable and alive with psychological complexity as anything in the revered director's output.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: It's a movie in which Campion, who shot it in her native New Zealand, works with a full-scale, at times painterly precision and control. It's also a socially conscious psychodrama that builds, over time, to a full boil.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: "The Power of the Dog" sticks its teeth into you so fast and furtively that you may not feel the sting on your skin until after the credits roll, but the delayed bite of the film's ending doesn't stop it from leaving behind a well-earned scar.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: Cumberbatch's magnificently unbridled nastiness deserves to be enjoyed on the biggest scale possible.
reviews.author: Raphael Abraham

reviews.text: Incrementally, by degrees, Campion shows the ways in which the men who set out to tame the frontier have instead been broken and bent to its will.
reviews.author: Xan Brooks

reviews.text: A powerful, ambiguous story about sibling rivalry, sexuality and self-hate.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: This is a psychosexual western to savor.
reviews.author: David Katz

reviews.text: Rich, thoughtful, visually and narratively compelling, The Power of The Dog proves once again why Jane Campion is one of the most interesting and respected filmmakers of our time.
reviews.author: Robert Ruggio

synopsis: Severe, pale-eyed, handsome, Phil Burbank is brutally beguiling. All of Phil's romance, power and fragility is trapped in the past and in the land: He can castrate a bull calf with two swift slashes of his knife; he swims naked in the river, smearing his body with mud. He is a cowboy as raw as his hides. The year is 1925. The Burbank brothers are wealthy ranchers in Montana. At the Red Mill restaurant on their way to market, the brothers meet Rose, the widowed proprietress, and her impressionable son Peter. Phil behaves so cruelly he drives them both to tears, reveling in their hurt and rousing his fellow cowhands to laughter -- all except his brother George, who comforts Rose then returns to marry her. As Phil swings between fury and cunning, his taunting of Rose takes an eerie form -- he hovers at the edges of her vision, whistling a tune she can no longer play. His mockery of her son is more overt, amplified by the cheering of Phil's cowhand disciples. Then Phil appears to take the boy under his wing. Is this latest gesture a softening that leaves Phil exposed, or a plot twisting further into menace?
